title: SA tighten grip as AUS trail by 170 runs after stumps on Day 4 in 2nd Test
description:
Travis Head led with 87 not out as Australia finished day four at 156-4 in its second innings in the second cricket test against South Africa on Wednesday, still trailing by 170 runs.
Head hit nine fours and faced 138 deliveries, with Scott Boland (2 not out) also on nightwatchman duty.
South Africa enforced the follow-on after Marco Jansen took 5-33 in Australia's first innings. The visitors were bowled out for 99 runs, conceding a lead of 326 runs in reply to the Proteas' 425-9 declared. Skipper Temba Bavuma had led South Africa's revival with a career-best 179.
It was the fourth lowest innings' total for Australia, and the third highest lead conceded in tests against South Africa.
Australia was down to 69-6 at lunch on day four, with Jansen picking four wickets in the morning session.
Jansen struck early in the morning after Australia started at 3-1 overnight. Boland was the first to go as he was caught behind off Jansen on the seventh ball of the day.
